record.provider: Utho Archive Storage (India) — ₹0.38/GB/mo cold tier, ₹-denominated, no egress fee

free_tier.stated: ₹0.38/GB/month, no minimum commitment, 11-nines designed durability, 1-4 hour standard retrieval (instant available). The general object tier is quoted separately at ₹4/GB/month above a 100 GB base.

egress.terms: «No egress fees in India» on the object-storage page and «Zero egress fees» / «No bandwidth overage charges» on the pricing page. The archive page itself says «No hidden retrieval fees». Utho's own pricing API, however, gives no bandwidth allowance per object plan (every plan's `bandwidth` field is 0), so the free-egress claim rests on marketing copy rather than a metered allowance. Record it as a claim, not a contract.

record.tooling: S3-compatible API with documented REST v2 endpoints (verified live: `GET https://api.utho.com/v2/pricing/objectstorage` -> 200, full plan ladder returned). boto3, rclone `s3`, Datashim. CDN-ready.
record.chaining: Per-GB with no cap, so 5 TB and 20 TB are the same rate. India-only regions (Noida/Mumbai).
record.limits_note: 1-4 hour retrieval on the standard path. This is archive, not the hot 10 TiB. The archive product page carries no S3 endpoint of its own and no explicit statement that it is S3-addressable, so it may be a bucket lifecycle class rather than a separate API. Volume pricing is not published: the ladder from the API stops at 10 TB, and 20 TB requires sales contact.
record.reliability_note: The most important reliability finding here is a PRICE DISCREPANCY INSIDE ONE VENDOR. Utho's marketing pages advertise object storage at «₹4/GB/month above 100 GB» and the pricing-comparison page claims «60-70 % More Affordable Than AWS», while Utho's own plan API returns ₹5.00/GB at 25 GB falling to ₹1.95/GB only at 10 TB. I.e. the advertised headline rate is roughly 2× the actual entry price and only reachable at the top of the ladder. Treat every Utho number as requiring an API cross-check. Node/uptime history not independently verified.
